item.content:encoded:
The SUSTAIN Seminar 2026 is inviting motivated young people from across Europe to participate in an international learning and networking event focused on strengthening rural youth organisations, developing sustainable youth networks, and increasing the participation of rural communities in decision-making.

Organised by Rural Youth Europe (RYE) and the Rural Youth Parliament in Slovakia (VPMS), the SUSTAIN Seminar will take place from 8 to 13 November 2026 in Hokovce, Slovakia, with the main seminar programme running from 9 to 12 November.

The event will bring together 25 young people from across Europe for peer learning, organisational development, policy engagement, networking and practical planning. The activity forms part of the Rural Youth Forward project, which is co-funded by the Erasmus+ Programme of the European Union.

SUSTAIN Seminar 2026 Overview

The SUSTAIN Seminar is designed for young people who are actively involved in rural communities, youth organisations, youth work, farming, community initiatives or networks and who want to learn how to make such organisations more resilient, representative and influential.

Participants will examine the challenges faced by rural youth organisations and explore practical approaches to:

  • Strengthen organisational structures.
  • Improve leadership and governance.
  • Engage and retain volunteers.
  • Develop sustainable financing models.
  • Build partnerships.
  • Improve communication.
  • Encourage generational renewal.
  • Increase youth participation in policy-making.
  • Connect grassroots concerns with national and European decision-making processes.

The seminar will use a highly participatory approach, allowing participants to learn from one another while developing practical solutions that can be applied in their own communities and organisations.

What Is the SUSTAIN Seminar?

The SUSTAIN Seminar is an international seminar focused on sustaining and growing local and national rural youth organisations and networks and strengthening their European dimension.

Rural youth organisations play an important role in creating opportunities for young people to participate in their communities and make their voices heard in decision-making. However, many organisations face challenges such as dependence on short-term funding, limited volunteer capacity, informal organisational structures and difficulties transferring knowledge between generations.

The SUSTAIN Seminar seeks to address these challenges by helping participants understand what is required not only to establish rural youth organisations, but also to maintain and grow them over the long term.

The event will bring together 25 selected participants for several days of peer learning, organisational reflection and practical policy work.

About the Rural Youth Forward Project

The SUSTAIN Seminar is organised within the Rural Youth Forward project, which aims to cultivate resilient rural youth networks capable of contributing to more inclusive and participatory policy-making.

The project recognises that young people in rural areas need meaningful opportunities to influence decisions affecting their communities.

Through activities such as research, study visits, mentoring and seminars, the project seeks to strengthen the ability of rural youth organisations to:

  • Represent the interests of rural young people.
  • Develop sustainable organisational structures.
  • Participate in policy processes.
  • Build stronger networks.
  • Create meaningful opportunities for youth participation.
  • Contribute to local, national and European policy discussions.

What Will Participants Learn?

The SUSTAIN Seminar has been designed around practical organisational and policy challenges.

Participants will explore several important areas.

1. Organisational Sustainability

Participants will examine what makes a rural youth organisation healthy, resilient and capable of operating effectively over time.

Areas of discussion will include:

  • Organisational vision.
  • Governance.
  • Membership.
  • Programmes and services.
  • Feedback mechanisms.
  • Risk management.
  • Knowledge transfer.
  • Organisational development.

The aim is to help participants identify strengths and weaknesses within their own organisations or initiatives and develop practical approaches for improvement.

2. Leadership and Volunteer Engagement

Strong leadership is essential to maintaining youth organisations, particularly where organisations depend heavily on volunteers.

The seminar will explore sustainable approaches to:

  • Leadership development.
  • Volunteer engagement.
  • Generational renewal.
  • Knowledge sharing.
  • Organisational growth.
  • Building stronger teams.

Participants will have opportunities to exchange experiences and learn from the approaches used by other rural youth organisations across Europe.

3. Financing and Partnerships

Financial sustainability is another important issue for rural youth organisations.

Participants will examine approaches to:

  • Sustainable financing.
  • Partnership development.
  • Organisational growth.
  • Communication.
  • Building relationships with relevant stakeholders.

The seminar will encourage participants to think beyond short-term project funding and consider how organisations can develop stronger and more sustainable foundations.

4. European Union Youth Participation Tools

Participants will also learn about and explore European participation mechanisms that can help rural young people engage in policy-making.

These include:

  • Have Your Say.
  • The European Citizens’ Initiative.
  • Citizens’ panels.
  • Public consultations.
  • Petitions to the European Parliament.

These tools can provide avenues through which young people can move from identifying challenges in their communities to contributing to wider policy discussions.

5. Civic Dialogue

The programme will include a Civic Dialogue with European and national stakeholders.

The dialogue will be supported by Europe Direct and an invited Team Europe expert.

This component will give participants an opportunity to engage directly with stakeholders and better understand how youth perspectives can be brought into policy discussions.

6. European Parliament Simulation

Participants will take part in a simulation of the European Parliament.

Through this activity, participants will experience elements of policy negotiation and collaborative decision-making while working toward a shared Rural Youth Resolution.

This provides a practical way to understand how different perspectives can be brought together to develop common policy positions.

7. Organisational Action Plans

The seminar will not focus only on discussion and theory.

Participants will work on practical organisational action plans and recommendations that can contribute to the final policy paper of the Rural Youth Forward project.

This means participants will have the opportunity to translate what they learn during the seminar into concrete ideas and actions for their organisations and communities.

Learning Approach

The SUSTAIN Seminar will use an interactive and participatory learning model.

Rather than relying solely on traditional presentations, the programme will combine several learning methods, including:

  • Short expert inputs.
  • Peer-to-peer exchange.
  • Case studies.
  • Organisational self-assessment.
  • Workshop stations.
  • Civic Dialogue.
  • Policy simulation.
  • Collaborative drafting.
  • Group discussions.
  • Practical organisational planning.

Participants will therefore be expected to actively contribute their own experiences, knowledge, ideas and perspectives.

Key Project Resources

Participants will work with two important outputs from the Rural Youth Forward project:

Recommendations to Support Meaningful Youth Participation in Rural Areas

This resource provides recommendations intended to strengthen meaningful participation by young people in rural communities.

Quality Standards for Piloting and Mentorship Systems

Participants will also work with quality standards developed around piloting and mentorship systems.

During the seminar, participants will examine these resources in relation to their own organisational realities and explore how they can be transformed into practical next steps.

Who Can Apply?

The SUSTAIN Seminar is aimed at young people who have a connection to rural communities and rural youth development.

The organisers are particularly interested in applicants who fall into one or more of the following categories:

  • Active members of Rural Youth Europe member organisations or partner organisations.
  • Rural young people involved in local groups or community initiatives.
  • Young farmers.
  • Young people involved in emerging rural organisations.
  • Members of national rural youth networks.
  • Youth workers.
  • Youth leaders.
  • Youth practitioners.
  • People supporting rural youth through NGOs.
  • People involved in informal youth groups.
  • Individuals working with public institutions supporting rural youth.

Applicants may have experience or an interest in:

  • Youth work.
  • Education.
  • Rural development.
  • Youth participation.
  • Organisational sustainability.
  • Policy-making.
  • Community development.

Age Requirement

Applicants should be between 18 and 30 years old at the time of the seminar.

SUSTAIN Seminar 2026 Dates

The event will take place according to the following schedule:

  • Arrival: 8 November 2026
  • Main seminar programme: 9–12 November 2026
  • Departure: 13 November 2026
  • Overall dates, including travel: 8–13 November 2026

Location

The seminar will take place in:

Hokovce, Slovakia

Hokovce will serve as the setting for the international gathering of rural youth representatives, youth workers, leaders and practitioners from across Europe.

Travel, Accommodation and Meals

The organisers will provide substantial support for selected participants.

Accommodation

Shared accommodation will be covered by the organisers.

Meals

All meals will be covered from dinner on 8 November through breakfast on 13 November 2026.

Travel Reimbursement

Travel to and from Hokovce will be reimbursed in accordance with the project’s travel guidelines.

Further information regarding travel arrangements and accommodation will be provided to selected participants.

Participation Fee

There is no participation fee for the SUSTAIN Seminar.

Applicants should nevertheless wait until their participation has been officially confirmed before making travel or other arrangements.

How to Apply for the SUSTAIN Seminar 2026

Interested applicants must complete the official application form.

                                                            APPLY HERE

Application deadline: 25 September 2026.

Participation is by selection only, meaning that completing the application does not automatically guarantee a place at the seminar.

Selected applicants will receive a confirmation email following the selection process.

Applicants are specifically advised not to make travel arrangements or other commitments until their participation has been confirmed.

Application Deadline

The deadline is:

25 September 2026

Applicants should ensure that their application is completed and submitted before the deadline.

Because participation is competitive and limited to only 25 participants, interested applicants are encouraged to prepare their applications early rather than waiting until the final day.

Important Information for Applicants

Before applying, prospective participants should make sure that they can satisfy the main participation requirements.

Applicants should be prepared to:

  1. Demonstrate a connection to rural communities.
  2. Show an interest or experience in rural youth work, community development, youth participation, organisational development or policy-making.
  3. Participate in the entire programme from 8–13 November 2026.
  4. Communicate and participate actively in English.
  5. Share relevant experiences, practices or perspectives with other participants.
  6. Demonstrate motivation to apply what they learn after the seminar.
  7. Wait for official confirmation before making travel arrangements.

Why This Seminar Matters for Rural Youth

Rural young people often face challenges related to access to opportunities, participation in decision-making, organisational resources and representation.

Youth organisations can help address these challenges by creating structures through which young people can organise, communicate their concerns and participate in community and policy processes.

However, simply creating an organisation is not enough. Organisations need sustainable leadership, effective governance, committed volunteers, reliable partnerships and mechanisms for transferring knowledge between generations.

The SUSTAIN Seminar therefore focuses on the longer-term question of how rural youth organisations can remain effective, representative and influential.

By bringing together participants from different European countries, the seminar also creates an environment in which young people can compare experiences and identify solutions that may be adapted to their own local contexts.

Networking and International Exposure

One of the important aspects of the SUSTAIN Seminar is the opportunity to meet other young people working on rural youth issues across Europe.

Participants can exchange experiences with:

  • Rural youth leaders.
  • Young farmers.
  • Youth workers.
  • Community activists.
  • NGO representatives.
  • Youth practitioners.
  • Members of rural youth networks.

This international environment can encourage new partnerships, ideas and approaches to rural youth development.

Practical Outcomes for Participants

The seminar is designed to produce practical results rather than only providing theoretical knowledge.

Participants will have opportunities to develop:

  • Organisational action plans.
  • Recommendations.
  • Policy ideas.
  • New approaches to youth participation.
  • Strategies for organisational sustainability.
  • Ideas for volunteer engagement.
  • Approaches to partnership development.
  • Knowledge of European participation mechanisms.

Participants are also encouraged to use their learning and networks to support concrete actions after the seminar.

Organisers

The SUSTAIN Seminar is organised by:

  • Rural Youth Europe (RYE)
  • Rural Youth Parliament in Slovakia (VPMS)

The activity forms part of the Rural Youth Forward project and is co-funded by the European Union through EACEA under the Erasmus+ programme.

Important Disclaimer

The activity is part of the Rural Youth Forward project, co-funded by the European Union through EACEA. The views and opinions expressed by the organisers and participants are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect the views of the European Union or EACEA. Neither the European Union nor the granting authority can be held responsible for them.

Learn more about this opportunity HERE

Conclusion

The SUSTAIN Seminar 2026 in Hokovce, Slovakia offers a valuable opportunity for young people involved in rural communities and youth development to strengthen their organisational, leadership and policy-making skills.

With 25 participants from across Europe, the seminar will combine peer learning, practical workshops, organisational assessment, policy engagement, Civic Dialogue and a European Parliament simulation. Participants will also have the opportunity to develop practical action plans and contribute to recommendations for strengthening rural youth organisations.

The organisers will cover shared accommodation and meals, while travel will be reimbursed according to the project’s travel guidelines. There is also no participation fee, making the opportunity accessible to eligible young people who are committed to rural youth development.

Those interested should ensure they meet the age, country, rural-community connection, English-language and participation requirements and submit their application by the 25 September 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship is an exciting funding opportunity for documentary filmmakers who want to tell compelling, cinematic stories about the rapidly evolving world of psychedelics.

The fellowship is designed to support filmmakers producing documentaries that explore the science, policy, business and culture surrounding psychedelics. Through substantial production funding, the program seeks to help a new generation of filmmakers bring important and underreported stories to audiences through film.

For 2026, the fellowship offers two different grant opportunities: a Feature-Length Documentary Grant providing up to $20,000 to selected filmmakers and a Short-Form Documentary Grant providing up to $10,000 to selected filmmakers.

The application deadline is October 5, 2026.

The fellowship is a project of the U.C. Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics and is intended to foster a diverse group of filmmakers documenting a field that is undergoing significant scientific, cultural, political and social change.

About the Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship

The psychedelic field is developing rapidly, with growing public interest in areas such as psychedelic-assisted therapy, scientific research, drug policy, cultural practices, business and emerging approaches to mental health and wellness.

The Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship seeks filmmakers capable of transforming these developments into strong cinematic narratives.

Rather than simply funding general filmmaking activities, the fellowship is interested in projects with compelling stories that can engage audiences while providing deeper insight into the issues surrounding psychedelics.

According to the fellowship, it is looking for groundbreaking narratives fit for cinematic storytelling, particularly untold stories that can illuminate the science, policy, business and culture of this emerging era.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to filmmakers who have identified an important story that has not yet received sufficient attention.

What Funding Is Available?

The fellowship has two distinct funding tracks.

1. Feature-Length Documentary Grant

The Feature-Length Documentary Grant will provide:

  • Up to $20,000 per filmmaker
  • Three documentary filmmakers will be selected
  • Funding can support the production or post-production of a feature-length documentary
  • The documentary must be more than 40 minutes in length
  • The project should be a documentary or nonfiction film rather than fiction.

The feature-length grant is particularly suited to filmmakers who already have a substantial documentary project underway and need additional resources to complete production or post-production.

The application materials indicate that applicants should be the director of the project, have relevant prior work samples, have access to participants and locations, and be independently producing the project.

What can the funding help with?

Depending on the project’s needs, documentary production funding can potentially help a filmmaker cover costs associated with completing the project, such as:

  • Production activities
  • Post-production
  • Filming
  • Editing
  • Other legitimate project-related costs
  • Costs necessary to move the documentary toward completion

The fellowship does not require grantees to submit individual expenses for reimbursement. However, successful applicants are expected to provide a report explaining how the grant was spent and what was accomplished on the project.

2. Short-Form Documentary Grant

The Short-Form Documentary Grant will provide:

  • Up to $10,000 per filmmaker
  • Up to five documentary filmmakers may be selected
  • Funding is intended for the production of short-form documentaries
  • The film must be 40 minutes or less

This track is particularly important for emerging filmmakers because it can provide meaningful financial support for a shorter documentary project.

The fellowship specifically encourages student filmmakers currently enrolled in graduate programs to consider the Short-Form Documentary Grant, although additional eligibility requirements apply to student applicants.

Special Opportunity for Student Filmmakers

Students should pay particular attention to the eligibility requirements because the fellowship does not treat student applications in the same way as applications from established independent filmmakers.

For the student route, eligible applicants must be enrolled in a U.S.-based undergraduate or graduate-level film or journalism program at an intermediate level or higher and must have a faculty advisor supporting the project. The faculty advisor must provide a letter of support by the application deadline.

The fellowship’s FAQ further clarifies that only graduate-school-level student films are eligible for the Short-Form Documentary Grant.

Therefore, prospective student applicants should carefully check the current application requirements before preparing their submission.

Important student restriction

A current student cannot apply for the Feature-Length Documentary Grant under the current rules.

Who Can Apply?

One of the most attractive aspects of this opportunity is its international eligibility.

The fellowship confirms that both grants are open to filmmakers worldwide, regardless of nationality or citizenship status.

This means filmmakers from:

  • Africa
  • Asia
  • Europe
  • North America
  • South America
  • Central America
  • The Caribbean
  • Oceania
  • Other parts of the world

may apply, provided they satisfy the relevant grant’s project and applicant requirements.

There is no stated nationality or citizenship restriction preventing international filmmakers from applying.

For example, a qualified documentary filmmaker based in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Uganda, Rwanda, India, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Brazil or another country can potentially apply.

However, being from an eligible country alone does not guarantee eligibility. Applicants must also meet the requirements for their chosen grant.

Eligibility Requirements for Documentary Filmmakers

For the feature-length production/post-production route, the application requirements indicate that applicants should satisfy several important criteria.

1. You must be the director

The applicant must be the director of the documentary project.

This is important because the funding is intended to support individual filmmakers who are directly responsible for the creative direction of the project.

2. You need relevant previous work

Applicants must have prior work samples in which they played a principal role, such as:

  • Director
  • Co-director
  • Producer
  • Co-producer

Therefore, applicants should be prepared to demonstrate their filmmaking experience through previous work samples.

3. The project must be documentary or nonfiction

The project must be a:

  • Documentary
  • Nonfiction film
  • Hybrid documentary

The fellowship does not support fiction films.

4. Feature projects must meet the required length

For the feature-length grant, the project must be at least 40 minutes in length according to the application materials.

5. The project should already be in production or post-production

The feature production/post-production grant is designed for projects that have progressed beyond the earliest development stage.

The application recommends that applicants have at least 10% of their footage shot by the application date, although applicants should consult the current FAQ for clarification about project stages.

6. You must have access to the story

Applicants must have confirmed access to:

  • Participants
  • Locations

This is important because the selection committee wants to see that the proposed documentary is realistically achievable.

7. The project must be independently produced

The documentary must be independently produced.

Works produced as “work for hire” are not eligible for the relevant production/post-production grant.

8. Only individuals can apply

Applications must come from individual filmmakers.

Organizations such as:

  • Universities
  • Foundations
  • Nonprofit businesses
  • Other organizations

cannot apply on behalf of a project.

What Types of Stories Is the Fellowship Looking For?

The fellowship is intentionally broad in its thematic scope.

It is interested in documentary stories examining different dimensions of psychedelics, including:

Science

Projects may explore scientific research and the developing understanding of psychedelic substances and their effects.

Policy

Filmmakers can examine laws, regulations, drug policy and the changing political environment surrounding psychedelics.

Business

Stories can investigate the growing commercial ecosystem surrounding psychedelic research, services, companies and related industries.

Culture

Documentaries may examine how psychedelics intersect with culture, communities, traditions and changing social attitudes.

The fellowship is particularly interested in untold and compelling narratives rather than generic treatments of the topic.

A strong application should therefore demonstrate why the proposed story matters and why audiences should care about it.

International Applicants Are Welcome

International filmmakers should take particular note of this opportunity.

The official FAQ explicitly states that filmmakers residing outside the United States can apply, and that both grants are open worldwide regardless of nationality or citizenship status.

Therefore, you do not have to be a U.S. citizen to apply.

However, international applicants should be aware that receiving fellowship funds may have tax implications, particularly for foreign nationals working in the United States. UC Berkeley may require documentation through its tax compliance process, and foreign nationals receiving fellowship payments may be subject to withholding depending on their circumstances.

Can the Documentary Be in Another Language?

Yes.

A filmmaker can produce a documentary in a language other than English, provided that the finished film will have English subtitles.

However, the application itself must be written in English because the selection committee does not have the capacity to evaluate applications in other languages.

This is particularly useful for filmmakers documenting psychedelic-related stories within communities where English is not the primary language.

Important Restrictions Applicants Should Know

Before applying, filmmakers should carefully consider several restrictions.

Fiction films are not eligible

The fellowship does not fund fiction films. The proposed project must be documentary, nonfiction or an eligible hybrid documentary.

Cannabis stories are not eligible

The fellowship’s FAQ states that it does not fund stories about cannabis and directs applicants to its definition of what qualifies as a psychedelic substance.

First-person illegal-substance experiences are not eligible

Applicants should not pitch stories centered on personally taking illegal substances and reporting on the experience. The fellowship specifically states that such stories cannot be supported for legal reasons.

Previously publicly distributed films are not eligible

A project that has already been publicly distributed is not eligible. This includes previous:

  • Theatrical screenings
  • Festival screenings
  • Educational screenings
  • Community screenings

Applicants should therefore ensure that the project they submit has not already been publicly distributed in these ways.

You cannot submit multiple stories

Each applicant may submit only one story pitch.

You cannot apply to both grant categories

Applicants must choose between the Feature-Length Documentary Grant and the Short-Form Documentary Grant.

You cannot apply to both grants during the same year.

Can Filmmakers Apply as a Team?

Yes, filmmakers can work with collaborators, co-directors or colleagues.

However, the fellowship requires one primary applicant to submit the application.

If awarded, the funds will be distributed to the primary applicant, who can then distribute funds to other members of the filmmaking team as appropriate.

This means a collaborative project does not necessarily have to be completed by one person, but the application needs to identify a primary applicant.

What Happens If You Are Selected?

Grant recipients have several responsibilities after receiving funding.

Successful fellows are expected to:

  1. Attend 3–4 virtual cohort meetings.
  2. Submit a written report within six months of the initial grant issuance.
  3. Explain how the grant money was spent.
  4. Describe what has been accomplished on the documentary.
  5. Share the finished film with the Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics once it is completed.
  6. Credit the Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship in the finished film.

Student filmmakers also have additional expectations relating to completion of their film as part of their graduate-level coursework and faculty-advisor supervision.

How Will the Grant Money Be Paid?

The payment structure differs between the two grants.

Feature-Length Documentary Grant

Feature-length awardees receive:

  • Half of the award upfront
  • The remaining half six months later, after completing a project-update memo.

Short-Form Documentary Grant

Short-form awardees receive:

  • The full grant amount upfront.

The fellowship does not require recipients to submit individual expenses for reimbursement, although a six-month report explaining spending and project progress is required.

Is There an Application Fee?

No.

The application is free to submit.

This makes the opportunity particularly accessible to emerging filmmakers who may not have substantial resources available for application fees.

What Should Applicants Prepare?

A strong application should be built around a compelling documentary idea and demonstrate that the filmmaker has the experience, access and ability to execute it.

Applicants should be prepared to provide information about areas such as:

  • The documentary’s working title
  • Project stage
  • Story concept
  • Topic and context
  • Filmmaker background
  • Previous work
  • Artistic approach
  • Connection to the story
  • Access to participants and locations
  • Funding received so far
  • Project budget
  • Production plans

The application materials also ask filmmakers to explain the creative and narrative direction of their projects.

For student applicants, the application includes areas such as a logline, topic summary, story or concept summary, filmmaker statement, artistic approach, connection and access, and funding to date.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Although no application can guarantee funding, filmmakers can strengthen their submissions by paying close attention to the fellowship’s priorities.

1. Lead with the story

Do not make the application simply a discussion about psychedelics.

Instead, identify the human story at the center of the documentary.

Explain who the audience will follow, what is at stake and why the story is important now.

2. Demonstrate cinematic potential

The fellowship specifically seeks narratives suitable for cinematic storytelling.

Explain what viewers will see, hear and experience.

3. Show that you have access

If your documentary depends on specific people, communities, locations or institutions, explain how you will access them.

4. Demonstrate your filmmaking ability

Previous work samples are important, particularly for applicants seeking the feature-length funding.

Choose work that demonstrates your ability to tell compelling nonfiction stories.

5. Make the project’s relevance clear

Explain why the story matters within the larger conversation around psychedelics.

Consider the scientific, cultural, political, economic or social implications of the story.

6. Be realistic about production

A compelling concept needs a credible execution plan.

Make sure your proposed budget and production strategy are realistic.

7. Follow the eligibility rules carefully

Do not submit a project that falls into one of the excluded categories, such as fiction, cannabis-focused stories or previously publicly distributed films.

8. Remember the language requirement

If your film will be produced in another language, plan for English subtitles and prepare the application in English.

Important Information for Applicants Working With Collaborators

If several people are developing the documentary together, applicants should decide who will serve as the primary applicant before submission.

The fellowship does not split the application into multiple primary applicants. One person should submit the application and receive the funds, with the primary applicant then able to distribute funds to other team members.

Can You Reapply?

Yes.

Applicants who are unsuccessful may reapply if their project has undergone significant new developments since the previous application.

If reapplying, filmmakers should clearly explain what has changed or progressed since their earlier submission.

When Will Applicants Hear Back?

According to the current FAQ, applicants will be notified of award decisions by December 2026.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship is:

October 5, 2026

Applicants should submit their materials before the deadline because the fellowship states that extensions cannot be provided.

Apply Here

Feature-Length Documentary Grant:
Apply for the Feature-Length Documentary Grant HERE

Short-Form Documentary Grant:

Apply for the Short-form Documentary Grant HERE

Quick Summary of the Opportunity

Feature Details
Opportunity Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship
Category Grant / Fellowship
Host U.C. Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics
Feature-Length Grant Up to $20,000
Number of Feature Grants 3
Short-Form Grant Up to $10,000
Number of Short-Form Grants Up to 5

Short Form 40 minutes or less
Eligible Applicants Individual documentary filmmakers
International Applicants Yes
Nationality Restriction None stated; worldwide eligibility
Student Applicants Eligible under specific requirements, particularly for short-form
Application Fee None
Application Deadline October 5, 2026
Decision Notification By December 2026
Application Online

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity could be particularly valuable for:

  • Independent documentary filmmakers
  • Nonfiction filmmakers
  • Documentary directors
  • Documentary producers who meet the primary-applicant requirements
  • Filmmakers researching the science of psychedelics
  • Filmmakers examining psychedelic policy
  • Filmmakers investigating the psychedelic business landscape
  • Filmmakers exploring the cultural dimensions of psychedelics
  • Filmmakers with compelling underreported stories
  • Graduate student filmmakers meeting the specific student requirements
  • International filmmakers from any country who satisfy the applicable eligibility requirements

The fellowship could be especially attractive to filmmakers who already have access to a compelling story and need financial support to take the project into production or complete post-production.

Learn more about this opportunity HERE

Conclusion

The Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship presents a significant funding opportunity for documentary filmmakers interested in exploring one of the world’s rapidly developing and increasingly debated fields.

With up to $20,000 available for feature-length documentaries and up to $10,000 for short-form documentaries, the program can provide valuable financial support for filmmakers seeking to transform important psychedelic-related stories into compelling cinematic work.

The fellowship is also notable for its worldwide eligibility, allowing qualified filmmakers to apply regardless of nationality or citizenship. At the same time, applicants must carefully distinguish between the two funding tracks, as the eligibility requirements differ, particularly for students.

For filmmakers with an original, well-developed and visually compelling documentary story about the science, policy, business or culture of psychedelics, this could be an opportunity worth serious consideration.

Deadline: October 5, 2026. Applicants should review the official requirements carefully and submit their application through the appropriate grant portal before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Association of Commonwealth Universities (ACU) Early Career Conference Grants 2026–27 provide financial support for emerging researchers and academics who want to attend and actively participate in academic conferences in Commonwealth countries outside their country of work.

For early career academics, conferences can be an important part of building a successful research and teaching career. They provide opportunities to present research to an international audience, learn about new developments in a field, exchange ideas with other researchers, establish professional connections and bring new knowledge back to their universities.

Through the Early Career Conference Grants, the ACU is offering seven grants of up to GBP 2,000 each to eligible early career researchers and academics at ACU member universities.

The funding can contribute towards major costs associated with conference participation, including conference registration, international travel, accommodation, visa expenses and travel and health insurance.

Applications for the 2026–27 round open on 18 August 2026 and close on 13 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC.

Overview of the ACU Early Career Conference Grants

The Early Career Conference Grants are designed to help emerging academics gain valuable international conference experience.

Attending an academic conference is more than simply travelling to an event. For researchers who are still establishing themselves in their academic careers, a conference can provide an opportunity to:

  • Present research findings to other academics and specialists.
  • Receive feedback on research ideas and findings.
  • Discover the latest developments in their area of research.
  • Develop international professional networks.
  • Identify potential research collaborators.
  • Learn from established academics and researchers.
  • Exchange knowledge and ideas with colleagues from other institutions.
  • Strengthen their academic profile.
  • Bring new knowledge and perspectives back to their home university.
  • Improve teaching and research through exposure to current developments in their discipline.

The ACU states that conference participation can have a significant impact on both emerging academics and the universities that employ them.

What Is the Association of Commonwealth Universities?

The Association of Commonwealth Universities (ACU) is an international network of universities across the Commonwealth. Its programmes and funding opportunities support collaboration, professional development, research and knowledge exchange among universities and academics.

The Early Career Conference Grants form part of this broader effort to support emerging researchers and enable academic communities to benefit from international exchange.

What Funding Is Available?

For the 2026–27 funding round, seven grants are available, with each grant providing a maximum of:

GBP 2,000 per awardee

The grant can be used to help cover eligible expenses connected with attending and participating in the proposed conference.

Eligible costs include:

  1. Conference registration feeFunding can contribute towards the cost of registering for the conference.
  2. FlightsThe grant can be used towards flight costs associated with travelling to the conference.
  3. AccommodationAwardees can use the funding to help cover accommodation expenses during the conference trip.
  4. Visa costsWhere a visa is required for travel to the conference country, visa expenses can be covered by the grant.
  5. Travel and health insuranceFunding can also contribute towards travel and health insurance associated with the conference trip.

Applicants should carefully review the official application guidance and FAQs for further information about eligible expenses and funding conditions before submitting an application.

Who Can Apply for the Early Career Conference Grant?

The grant is specifically intended for early career researchers and academics at ACU member universities.

Applicants must satisfy the eligibility requirements established for the programme.

1. Applicants must be early career researchers or academics

An applicant must be an early career researcher or academic working at an ACU member university.

For the purposes of this grant, early career researchers and academics are generally defined as those who are within seven years of the start of their academic research or teaching career.

This means that applicants should consider when they began their academic research or teaching career when determining whether they fall within the seven-year early career period.

2. Career breaks may be considered

The seven-year criterion does not necessarily exclude applicants who have experienced a career break.

The ACU recognises that researchers and academics may take time away from employment for personal or professional reasons.

Examples of career breaks can include periods away from employment to:

  • Care for children.
  • Address personal circumstances.
  • Take time away from academic employment for professional reasons.
  • Deal with other circumstances that result in a temporary period away from employment.

Applicants who have experienced a career break should review the official guidance to determine how their circumstances affect their eligibility.

Applicants Must Identify a Suitable Conference

Applicants must identify a conference that they would like to attend as part of their application.

The proposed conference must satisfy important requirements.

The conference must take place in a Commonwealth country

The conference must be held in a Commonwealth country.

In addition, the conference must take place outside the applicant’s country of work.

This requirement makes the grant particularly valuable for academics seeking international exposure and opportunities to engage with researchers in other Commonwealth countries.

Conference dates

The proposed conference must take place between:

February 2027 and January 2028

Applicants should therefore identify a suitable conference falling within this period before submitting their application.

Applicants Must Actively Participate in the Conference

Simply attending a conference is not sufficient for this grant.

Applicants must have an active role in the proposed conference.

They must be doing at least one of the following:

  • Chairing a session
  • Presenting a paper
  • Presenting a poster

This requirement means applicants should already have identified an appropriate opportunity to contribute academically to the conference.

Researchers should therefore consider conferences that are directly relevant to their research interests and where they can demonstrate an active contribution.

Why Conference Participation Matters for Early Career Researchers

Academic conferences can be particularly valuable during the early stages of a research career.

For researchers who are still developing their academic networks and professional reputation, presenting at an international conference can create opportunities that may not be available through their normal university environment.

Conference participation can help early career academics to:

Share research

Presenting a paper or poster allows researchers to communicate their findings to academics working in related areas.

The feedback received during conference discussions can also help researchers identify strengths, weaknesses and potential improvements in their research.

Learn about new developments

Academic disciplines continuously evolve. Conferences bring together researchers who are working on current issues and emerging areas of research.

Participation can therefore help early career researchers remain informed about developments in their field.

Build professional networks

Meeting academics from other universities and countries can help researchers establish professional relationships that may continue after the conference.

These connections can potentially lead to research collaboration, knowledge exchange and other academic opportunities.

Strengthen research and teaching

Knowledge acquired through conference participation can be shared with colleagues and students at the researcher’s home university.

The benefits of the grant can therefore extend beyond the individual awardee and contribute to the wider academic community.

Important Ineligibility Conditions

Although the grant is intended to support international conference participation, there are important restrictions that applicants must understand.

Applicants must not have previously travelled outside their region of employment for work purposes

Applicants cannot have previously travelled outside their region of employment for work purposes, including conferences, since the start of their academic career.

This is an important eligibility requirement.

Applicants who have already travelled internationally for work or conference purposes during their academic career should carefully check the ACU’s definition of the relevant employment region and the application guidance before applying.

Previous ACU grant recipients cannot apply

Applicants who have previously received an ACU Early Career Conference Grant are not eligible to receive another award under this programme.

The programme was previously known as the Early Career Academic Grants, so previous recipients of the earlier version of the grant are also excluded.

Application Requirements

Before applying, prospective applicants should ensure they have identified an appropriate conference and understand the programme requirements.

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate that:

  • They are an early career researcher or academic.
  • They work at an ACU member university.
  • Their academic career falls within the applicable seven-year period, taking eligible career breaks into consideration.
  • They have identified a suitable conference.
  • The conference is taking place in a Commonwealth country.
  • The conference is outside their country of work.
  • The conference will take place between February 2027 and January 2028.
  • They will actively participate by chairing a session, presenting a paper or presenting a poster.
  • They meet the ACU’s requirements concerning previous international work travel.
  • They have not previously received an ACU Early Career Conference Grant or its previous Early Career Academic Grant equivalent.

How to Apply for the ACU Early Career Conference Grant

Applications are submitted online through the ACU application system.

APPLY HERE

Applicants can also visit the official website HERE

Applicants should first review the official application guidance and frequently asked questions before completing the application.

 

Applicants with an existing MyACU account

If you already have a MyACU account, you can access the application form through the ACU’s online grant application system.

Applicants without a MyACU account

Applicants who do not already have a MyACU account must first register for an account.

After registering, applicants should follow the instructions contained in the registration email to log into the system and access the application form.

Applicants should ensure that they provide accurate information and carefully follow the application instructions.

Application Timeline

The application period for the 2026–27 Early Career Conference Grants is:

Applications open: 18 August 2026

Applications close: 13 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC

Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing early rather than waiting until the final day.

This is particularly important because applicants need to identify an appropriate conference and demonstrate that they will actively participate through a presentation, poster or session chairing role.

Conference Period

The conference proposed in the application must take place between:

February 2027 and January 2028

Applicants should therefore look for conferences whose dates fall within this specified period.

Grant Conditions After Selection

Successful applicants will have responsibilities after receiving the grant.

All awardees are required to complete a report after completion of their award.

This reporting requirement means recipients should retain relevant information and documentation associated with their funded conference participation and be prepared to report on their experience and use of the award.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although meeting the eligibility criteria is essential, applicants can also take practical steps to make their applications clear and well prepared.

1. Choose a conference closely connected to your research

Select a conference that is directly relevant to your research or academic work.

A strong connection between your research and the conference can help demonstrate why participation would be valuable.

2. Confirm your participation role

Do not select a conference simply because it is interesting.

The programme requires applicants to actively participate by:

  • Chairing a session;
  • Presenting a paper; or
  • Presenting a poster.

Applicants should therefore have a clear understanding of their intended role.

3. Check the conference location

Confirm that the conference is being held in a Commonwealth country outside your country of work.

This is one of the central requirements of the grant.

4. Check the conference dates

Make sure the conference takes place between February 2027 and January 2028.

5. Confirm your university’s ACU membership

Before investing significant time in the application, verify that your university is an ACU member university.

6. Review the eligibility restrictions carefully

Applicants should pay particular attention to the rules concerning previous international work-related travel and previous receipt of an ACU Early Career Conference Grant.

7. Prepare early

Because applications close at a specific UTC time, applicants should avoid submitting at the last minute.

Early preparation also gives applicants time to review their information, confirm conference details and resolve any account or application issues.

Benefits of the Early Career Conference Grant

The ACU Early Career Conference Grant can provide several important benefits to emerging academics.

Financial support

The grant provides up to GBP 2,000, helping reduce the financial barriers associated with international conference participation.

International academic exposure

Participating in a conference in another Commonwealth country can expose researchers to different academic communities, approaches and research perspectives.

Research presentation experience

Applicants can gain experience presenting their research through papers or posters or by chairing academic sessions.

Professional networking

International conferences provide opportunities to meet academics, researchers and potential collaborators from different institutions.

Knowledge exchange

Awardees can bring knowledge gained at the conference back to their universities and share it with colleagues and students.

Career development

Conference participation can contribute to the professional development of early career researchers by increasing their exposure to the wider academic community.

Important Dates at a Glance

Item Details
Grant ACU Early Career Conference Grants
Number of grants 7
Maximum funding GBP 2,000 per grant
Applications open 18 August 2026
Application deadline 13 October 2026
Closing time 15:00 UTC
Eligible conference period February 2027 – January 2028
Conference location Commonwealth country outside country of work
Required participation Chairing a session, presenting a paper or presenting a poster
Post-award requirement Completion of an award report

Final Thoughts

The ACU Early Career Conference Grants 2026–27 represent a valuable opportunity for emerging researchers and academics to gain international conference experience without having to personally cover all of the associated travel and participation costs.

With seven grants of up to GBP 2,000, successful applicants can receive financial support for conference registration, flights, accommodation, visa expenses, and travel and health insurance.

More importantly, the programme can help early career academics share their research, learn about developments in their disciplines, establish professional networks and bring new knowledge back to their universities.

However, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The applicant must be an early career researcher or academic at an ACU member university, the conference must be in a Commonwealth country outside the applicant’s country of work, and the applicant must actively participate by chairing a session, presenting a paper or presenting a poster.

Applicants should also check the restrictions relating to previous international work-related travel and previous receipt of an ACU Early Career Conference Grant.

With applications closing on 13 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC, eligible researchers should begin preparing their conference plans and application well in advance of the deadline.
